private_notes.observations: No prior rate cards or hour allocations are available. Delivery cost is $200 per hour, and Meridian favors lower-priced firms.
private_notes.plan: Start with a competitive rate that preserves a meaningful margin. Use subsequent rate cards and allocated hours to estimate price sensitivity and adjust independently to maximize long-run profit.

private_notes.observations: No prior rates, allocations, or demand data are available. Fully loaded cost is $200 per hour.
private_notes.plan: Start with a competitive rate that maintains a meaningful margin. Use subsequent rate cards and observed hours to estimate demand sensitivity and adjust for long-run profit.

private_notes.observations: No rate cards or allocation data are available yet. Our fully loaded cost is $200 per hour, and both our relative rate and the panel's overall rates affect allocated hours.
private_notes.plan: Start at a moderate margin and use subsequent rate cards and allocated hours to estimate how our price affects profit. Adjust based on observed results rather than assuming competitors' prices or Meridian's allocation formula.

private_notes.observations: At $350 in Q1, we received 349 hours despite charging more than both other firms ($325 and $300). One quarter does not establish how sensitive allocations are to price.
private_notes.plan: Test a modest reduction to $325, matching one panel firm while retaining a $125 hourly margin. Compare next quarter's hours and rate card before making further adjustments.

private_notes.observations: At $325 in Q1, we received 575 hours and earned about $71,872. The other panel rates were $300 and $350; one quarter does not establish how sensitive our allocation is to price.
private_notes.plan: Raise the rate modestly to $330 to test whether a higher margin offsets any loss of hours. Compare Q2 hours and profit with Q1 before making a larger adjustment.

private_notes.observations: In Q1, a $300 rate yielded 948 hours and about $94,798 profit. Competitors charged $325 and $350. There is not yet enough data to estimate how a rate increase would affect our allocated hours.
private_notes.plan: Raise the rate modestly to test demand while remaining below both competitors’ most recently published rates. Use the resulting hours and next rate card to refine future pricing.

private_notes.observations: Reducing our rate from $350 in Q1 to $325 in Q2 coincided with hours rising from 349 to 597 and quarterly profit rising from $52,311 to $74,641. Competitors' latest rates were $330 and $315, so our Q2 rate sat between them. The allocation formula and competitors' future rates remain unknown.
private_notes.plan: Set $320 to test whether a small reduction increases allocated hours enough to outweigh the $5 lower margin per hour. At this rate, approximately 622 hours would match Q2 profit. Reassess after seeing Q3 hours and the panel rate card.

private_notes.observations: Raising our rate from $325 to $330 coincided with hours falling from 575 to 540 and quarterly profit declining slightly. Competitors’ average rate also fell from $325 to $320, so the effect of our rate change alone is unclear.
private_notes.plan: Return to $325 to test whether a more competitive position restores enough hours to improve profit. Avoid a larger cut until there is evidence it would pay off.

private_notes.observations: At $315 in Q2, profit fell to $83,873 from $94,798 at $300 in Q1. Allocated hours dropped substantially, though competitor rate changes also contributed.
private_notes.plan: Lower the rate to $305 to test whether recovering hours outweighs the smaller margin. Reassess after the next allocation and rate card.

private_notes.observations: Q2's $325 rate generated the highest quarterly profit ($74,641). Lowering the rate to $320 in Q3 did not increase allocated hours; hours fell from 597 to 579, while competitors also lowered their rates.
private_notes.plan: Return to $325. Monitor the next allocation and rate card to assess whether the Q3 decline reflected competitors' pricing rather than our $5 rate change.

private_notes.observations: At $325, allocated hours fell from 575 in Q1 to 524 in Q3 while both competitors lowered their rates. The Q2 increase to $330 produced slightly less profit than Q1, but changes in competitor rates make the effect of our own rate uncertain.
private_notes.plan: Test a modest increase to $335 rather than cut aggressively. Compare next quarter's hours and profit with the panel rate card before making a larger adjustment.

private_notes.observations: At $305 in Q3, hours rose to 781 from 729 in Q2 at $315, but quarterly profit fell from about $83,873 to $82,009. Both rivals also lowered rates, so the effect of our rate change is uncertain. Q1 at $300 generated the highest profit, though rivals charged more then.
private_notes.plan: Set $300 to improve competitiveness without sacrificing much margin. Compare Q4 hours and profit with Q3, accounting for changes in rivals’ rates before making another adjustment.

private_notes.observations: At $325, quarterly profit was $74,641 in Q2 and $67,740 in Q4. Lowering to $320 in Q3 produced $69,433; $350 in Q1 produced substantially less profit.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $325. The Q4 decline at the same rate suggests allocations also depend on rival pricing or demand. Monitor future hours and rate cards before making another adjustment.

private_notes.observations: The $335 rate in Q4 coincided with a decline to 444 hours and about $59,898 in profit, versus 524 hours and about $65,443 at $325 in Q3. Both competitors charged less than us in Q4.
private_notes.plan: Lower the rate enough to improve our position relative to Arden & Cole without sacrificing too much margin. Assess the resulting hours and profit next quarter; the allocation formula and competitors' future rates remain uncertain.

private_notes.observations: At $300, quarterly profit was approximately $94,798 in Q1 and $89,347 in Q4. The higher $305 and $315 rates produced lower profits, although competitors’ rates also changed.
private_notes.plan: Maintain $300 this quarter. It has delivered the strongest observed profits; reassess after seeing the next allocation and rate card.

private_notes.observations: At $325, allocated hours fell from 597 in Q2 to 489 in Q5 as rival pricing became less favorable. Q5's $325 rate exceeded both competitors' rates ($315 and $300).
private_notes.plan: Lower the rate to $315 to improve competitiveness while preserving a $115-per-hour margin. Compare next quarter's allocation with Q5 to assess whether the added hours offset the lower margin.

private_notes.observations: Q5's $315 rate increased hours to 597, but quarterly profit remained below Q1 and Q2. Higher rates in Q3–Q4 coincided with fewer hours, though competitor rates and demand also changed.
private_notes.plan: Set a $320 rate to recover some margin while remaining below Arden & Cole's latest published rate. Compare the resulting hours and profit with Q5 before adjusting again.

private_notes.observations: At $300, quarterly profits were approximately $94.8k, $89.3k, and $80.6k, exceeding the observed profits at $305 and $315. Q5 hours fell as Birchwood lowered its rate to $315, but $300 remains the best-supported choice.
private_notes.plan: Maintain $300 and reassess after Q6 allocation and competitor rates are published.

private_notes.observations: At $315 in Q6, we received 582 hours and earned $66,911, versus 489 hours and $61,076 at $325 in Q5. The added hours more than offset the lower margin, although Birchwood Hale’s rate also rose by $5.
private_notes.plan: Test a modest further reduction to $310. It needs roughly 608 hours to outperform Q6’s profit. Use the next allocation and rate card to assess whether the additional volume justifies the lower margin.

private_notes.observations: Q6 profit fell to $63,176 at $320, versus $68,631 at $315 in Q5. Arden & Cole lowered its rate to $315 in Q6; Calder Rowe remained at $300. The data do not isolate the effect of our rate change from competitors' changes.
private_notes.plan: Return to $315 to improve competitiveness while preserving a $115 hourly margin. Compare Q7 hours and profit with prior quarters before making a larger adjustment.

private_notes.observations: At $300, allocated hours declined from 893 in Q4 to 785 in Q6 as competing rates generally fell. Q6 rates were $315 and $320; our profit was $78,540.
private_notes.plan: Lower the rate modestly to improve our share as competitors' rates decline, then assess whether the additional hours offset the smaller margin.

private_notes.observations: The cut from $315 to $310 raised hours only from 582 to 585, reducing quarterly profit from about $66,900 to $64,300. Recent rate cards show both competitors also lowering rates.
private_notes.plan: Return to $315 to recover margin without moving far above competitors. Monitor whether hours remain near Q6's level; avoid further cuts unless they produce substantially more volume.

private_notes.observations: At $315 in Q7, Birchwood Hale earned $60,852 on 529 hours. Both competing firms have lowered their rates, and our hours fell despite holding our rate at $315.
private_notes.plan: Lower the rate modestly to improve competitiveness without sacrificing much hourly margin. Compare the resulting hours and profit with Q7 before making a larger change.

private_notes.observations: The Q7 cut from $300 to $295 did not materially increase hours: 789 versus 785 in Q6, while quarterly profit fell. Competitors have also lowered their rates, making earlier high-volume quarters less directly comparable.
private_notes.plan: Reverse the unproductive rate cut and test a modest increase to $305. Monitor whether the added margin outweighs any loss of hours before making further adjustments.

private_notes.observations: At $315 in Q8, we received 570 hours and earned $65,541. Previous quarters at $325 produced profits ranging from $61,076 to $74,641, depending on competitors’ rates. Further cuts have not consistently generated enough additional hours to offset the lower margin.
private_notes.plan: Raise the rate modestly to $320 to test whether we can recover margin while retaining a competitive share of hours. Reassess after seeing the Q9 allocation and panel rate card.

private_notes.observations: At $310 in Q8, we received 630 hours and earned $69,285, up from 529 hours and $60,852 at $315 in Q7. Allocation varies across quarters, so the gain cannot be attributed entirely to our rate change.
private_notes.plan: Test a modest further reduction to $305. Compare the resulting hours and profit with Q8 before deciding whether to lower the rate again or restore it.

private_notes.observations: At $305 in Q8, profit was $73,091 on 696 hours, down from $74,992 at $295 in Q7. Competing rates also fell, so the change in hours cannot be attributed solely to our increase.
private_notes.plan: Set $300 to improve our competitiveness without returning to the $295 rate. Compare the resulting hours and profit with Q8 before adjusting again.

private_notes.observations: At $320 in Q9, profit fell to $59,353 as the other firms posted $305 and $300. Our strongest recent profits came at $315 when our rate was closer to the panel.
private_notes.plan: Lower the rate to $310 to regain hours while maintaining a $110 margin per hour. Reassess after the Q10 allocation and rate card; avoid repeated cuts unless the additional hours justify them.

private_notes.observations: At $305 in Q9, profit was $70,104, slightly above Q8's $69,285 at $310. The additional hours more than offset the lower margin, though competitor rates also changed.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $305 to test whether Q9's strong allocation persists. Avoid another cut until there is clearer evidence it would improve long-run profit.

private_notes.observations: At $300 in Q9, profit rose slightly from Q8 despite a declining-hours trend. The $295 rate in Q7 did not produce enough additional hours to justify its lower margin.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $300. Reassess if future allocations show a sustained change in demand or competitors' rates.

private_notes.observations: At $310 in Q10, Arden & Cole earned $63,003 on 573 hours, up from $59,353 at $320 in Q9. Competitor rates remained near $300–$305.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $310. The Q10 reduction improved profit, but the evidence does not yet justify another cut that would narrow our margin and risk further price competition.

private_notes.observations: At $305, the last two quarters delivered 668 and 633 hours, producing $70,104 and $66,465 in profit. Nearby higher rates have not consistently improved profit, though competitor rates also varied.
private_notes.plan: Keep $305 for another quarter. This preserves a competitive position without cutting margin; reassess if allocations or the panel rate card change materially.

private_notes.observations: At $300, quarterly profit has declined from about $89,000 in Q4 to $70,000 in Q10. Recent panel rates are lower than in early quarters, and the allocation formula is unknown. The Q8 increase to $305 did not clearly improve profit relative to nearby quarters.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $300 this quarter. Continue comparing profit and allocated hours across quarters, accounting for changes in panel rates and overall demand before adjusting.

private_notes.observations: At $310, we received 573 hours and earned $63,003 in both Q10 and Q11. Both competitors also held their rates steady at $305 and $300.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $310. The stable allocation provides no new evidence that a further cut would improve long-run profit enough to justify its lower margin or potential competitive response.

private_notes.observations: At $305, allocated hours held steady at 633 in Q10 and Q11, producing $66,465 profit each quarter. The other firms' rates also remained unchanged at $310 and $300.
private_notes.plan: Maintain $305 to preserve a competitive position and a $105 margin per hour. Reassess if allocation or competitors' rates change.

private_notes.observations: At $300 with competitors at $310 and $305, Calder Rowe received 700 hours and approximately $69,957 profit in each of Q10 and Q11. Earlier quarters had higher allocations, but competitor rates and likely demand also differed, so they do not establish that a price cut would improve profit.
private_notes.plan: Hold the $300 rate rather than initiate a price-cutting cycle on uncertain evidence. Reassess if the panel rate card or allocated hours change materially.

private_notes.observations: At $310, with competitors at $305 and $300, allocation and profit have remained stable for three quarters at 573 hours and approximately $63,003 per quarter. Recent higher rates produced lower profits.
private_notes.plan: Maintain $310. Reassess if competitors change rates or allocated hours shift; avoid cutting margin without evidence that additional hours would offset it.

private_notes.observations: At $305 with competitors at $310 and $300, allocation has held at 633 hours for three consecutive quarters, producing $66,465 profit each quarter. Higher relative rates have generally reduced allocated hours.
private_notes.plan: Maintain $305 while the panel rate card and allocation remain stable. Reassess if competitors change rates or Meridian's allocation shifts.

private_notes.observations: At $300, allocated hours and profit have held steady at 700 hours and approximately $70,000 for three quarters. Competitor rates have also remained unchanged at $310 and $305.
private_notes.plan: Maintain $300 rather than risk a price-cutting cycle. Reassess if allocations or competitor rates change.

private_notes.observations: At $310 with competitors at $305 and $300, Arden & Cole received 573 hours and earned $63,003 in each of the last four quarters. The panel rates and allocation have remained stable.
private_notes.plan: Maintain $310 to preserve the established profit level. Reassess if competitor rates or allocated hours change; avoid initiating a price cut without evidence of a sustained profit gain.

private_notes.observations: For Q10–Q13, all panel rates and our allocation remained unchanged: our $305 rate yielded 633 hours and $66,465 profit each quarter.
private_notes.plan: Maintain $305 while allocation and competitor rates remain stable. Reassess if either changes.

private_notes.observations: At $300, Calder Rowe has received approximately 700 hours and $69,957 profit in each of the last four quarters, while competitors' rates remained at $310 and $305. Earlier rate changes do not establish a clear improvement over this stable outcome.
private_notes.plan: Maintain $300 while allocations and competitor rates remain stable. Reassess if either changes materially.

private_notes.observations: With competitors at $305 and $300, our $310 rate produced 573 hours and about $63,003 profit each quarter from Q10–Q13. Cutting to $274 in Q14 increased allocation to 904 hours and profit to $66,880.
private_notes.plan: Test an intermediate rate to improve margin while retaining much of the volume gained in Q14. Adjust based on the resulting hours and competitor rates.

private_notes.observations: Arden & Cole cut its rate from $310 to $274 in Q14, while Calder Rowe stayed at $300. At our unchanged $305 rate, allocated hours fell from 633 to 486 and profit fell from $66,465 to $51,049.
private_notes.plan: Lower our rate to recover some allocation without matching Arden's sharp cut. Monitor next quarter's hours and panel rates, then adjust based on realized profit rather than hours alone.

private_notes.observations: Arden & Cole cut its rate from $310 to $274 in Q14, while our rate stayed at $300 and our allocated hours fell from 700 to 537. Birchwood Hale remained at $305. The allocation change warrants revisiting our rate.
private_notes.plan: Lower the rate moderately to regain hours without matching Arden's $274. Assess the resulting allocation and next quarter's rate card before making another change.

private_notes.observations: Q14’s $274 rate produced 904 hours with competitors at $305 and $300. In Q15, our $285 rate produced 666 hours as competitors fell to $290 and $285. The estimated profit-maximizing rate at current competitor prices is approximately $283.
private_notes.plan: Set $282, near the estimated profit maximum. Reassess after observing Q16 hours and the new panel rate card.

private_notes.observations: At $290 in Q15, profit was $54,198, up from $51,049 at $305 in Q14. Both other firms charged $285 in Q15, so our modest premium still attracted 602 hours.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $290 rather than make another cut based on one quarter. Track profit and allocation as panel rates stabilize; adjust only if the premium persistently reduces profit.

private_notes.observations: At $285 in Q15, we received 666 hours and earned $56,571, up from $53,732 at $300 in Q14. The latest competing rates are $285 and $290; allocation has declined substantially from earlier quarters.
private_notes.plan: Test a modest increase to $290 to improve margin while remaining competitive. Review the resulting hours and next rate card before adjusting further.

private_notes.observations: Q16 at $282 earned $58,598 on 715 hours with both competitors at $290. Q14 earned $66,880 at $274, but competitors then charged $300 and $305. Lower competitor rates have reduced the apparent benefit of deep discounting.
private_notes.plan: Raise the rate moderately to improve margin while remaining close to competitors. Reassess the hours response and next rate card before making a larger move.

private_notes.observations: At $290 in Q15–Q16, profit was about $54,000 per quarter. Competitors' latest rates were $282 and $290. Earlier $305 rates produced higher profit when competitors also charged more, but Q14 shows that a large premium over a competitor can sharply reduce allocated hours.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $290 while monitoring allocation and competitors' rates. Avoid a further cut without evidence that it would increase profit; reassess if competitors' rates or our allocated hours shift materially.

private_notes.observations: At $290 in Q16, profit fell to $54,806 from $56,571 at $285 in Q15. Arden & Cole’s latest rate was $282, below ours; Birchwood Hale’s was $290.
private_notes.plan: Set $280 to regain a competitive position and test whether the additional hours outweigh the lower margin. Reassess after seeing Q17 allocation and the next rate card.

private_notes.observations: At $295 in Q17, hours fell to 559 and profit to $53,110 while rival rates were $290 and $280. Earlier, rates near $280–$285 produced higher hours and profits, though competitor rates differed.
private_notes.plan: Set $280 to match the lowest current rival rate and seek more hours without sacrificing too much margin. Reassess after the next allocation and rate card.

private_notes.observations: At $290, allocated hours rose from 602 to 618 over Q15–Q17, with quarterly profit rising to $55,606. Earlier $305 rates earned more when competitors' rates were higher; the recent lower competitor rates make a return to $305 less attractive.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $290. Monitor allocation and the published rate card next quarter; adjust only if the evidence suggests a change would improve profit.

private_notes.observations: Q17's $280 rate won 755 hours, but profit of $60,371 remained below the roughly $70,000 earned at $300 when competitors charged $305–$310. Recent competitor rates are lower, at $290 and $295.
private_notes.plan: Raise modestly to $290 to improve margin while remaining competitive with the latest panel rates. Reassess the hours and competitor responses next quarter.

private_notes.observations: At $280 against two $290 rivals, we earned $58,647 on 733 hours. At $282 against the same rival rates, profit was nearly identical ($58,598 on 715 hours). Recent higher rates have produced lower profits.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $280. The observed $280–$282 range offers similar profit; avoid a further cut without evidence it would improve returns. Reassess when the next allocation and rate card arrive.

private_notes.observations: At $290, recent allocations have been stable at 600–618 hours, producing roughly $54,000–$56,000 in quarterly profit. The $305 rate performed poorly when a rival cut its rate substantially.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $290. Avoid provoking further rate cuts; reassess after seeing the next allocation and panel rate card.

private_notes.observations: At $290 in Q18, we earned $54,018 on 600 hours while Arden priced at $280. At $280 in Q17, we earned $60,371 on 755 hours. Recent results favor regaining hours over maintaining the higher margin.
private_notes.plan: Set $280 to match Arden's latest rate and undercut Birchwood's $290. Reassess profit and allocation after the next rate card.

private_notes.observations: At $280, profit was $58,647 with rival rates of $290/$290 and $54,993 with rival rates of $290/$280. Recent higher rates have generally earned less, while the $274 result benefited from higher rival rates.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $280. Recent results do not establish that a further cut would improve profit; reassess after the next allocation and rate card.

private_notes.observations: At $290, allocated hours fell to 563 in Q19 as both competitors priced at $280, reducing quarterly profit to about $50,653. Recent competitor rates have fluctuated between $280 and $295.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $290 rather than initiate another rate cut. Monitor whether competitors remain at $280 and reassess the profit trade-off after the next allocation.

private_notes.observations: At $280 in Q19, profit was about $55,000; at $290 with the same competing rates in Q18, it was about $54,000. Historically, $300 produced substantially higher profit when competitors charged over $300.
private_notes.plan: Test a return to $300. The recent allocation data suggest the higher margin may offset fewer hours, while a higher posted rate could help avoid a prolonged race to the bottom. Reassess after the next allocation and rate card.
